function: CMNN regresses the digital precoders of hybrid beamforming for O-RAN mmWave MU massive MIMO, imitating the iterative SCA-SOCP solution (Alg. 1) to maximize sum spectral efficiency (pp. 8-9).
system: Downlink MU mmWave massive MIMO, 6 cells, 2 O-RUs and 3 UEs per cell; NT=128, NR=8 antennas; 28 GHz, 100 MHz; no RIS (pp. 11-12, Table III).
method: Convolutional multi-output neural network (3 conv layers, 3 FC layers); supervised MSE regression on labels from the optimization Alg. 1, trained offline with Adam (pp. 9-10).
data_channel: Simulated narrow-band Saleh-Valenzuela mmWave channel with path loss 128.1+37.6log10(d), S=4 paths, uniform AoA/AoD; 300000 training and 20000 test samples; no public or measured data (pp. 5, 11).
test_conditions: Trained on CSI imperfection 0-1 and speeds 0-200 km/h (pp. 10-11); tested at CSI levels 0.25, 0.55 (off-grid) and at 240 km/h, outside the trained speeds (pp. 14-15).
baselines: Non-learned only: LS [6], SVD [43], BD [57] digital precoders; analog benchmark ABB [58]; own optimization Alg. 1 as reference; no learned baseline (pp. 11-12).
metrics: Cell throughput (Gbps), UE spectral efficiency (CDF and average), achievable sum-SE, training and validation MSE, FLOPs, CPU execution time (pp. 12-14).
complexity: FLOPs formula for CMNN (p. 11), Fig. 8: independent of NT; CPU time 22.3 ms versus 17.3 s for Alg. 1 at L=6, NT=64 (Table V, p. 13).
q1_support: p. 5: "We adopt the narrow-band geometric Saleh–Valenzuela channel model for the considered mmWave system". Custom simulated channel (path loss 128.1+37.6log10(d), S=4 paths); no 3GPP TR 38.901, DeepMIMO, QuaDRiGa or measured data is named.
q2_support: p. 15: "vmax = 240 km/h falls outside the range of vmax in the input features", where the CMNN still performs well; training speeds were "0 to 200 km/h" (p. 11).
q3_support: p. 11: "employ least squares (LS) [6], SVD [43], and block diagonalization (BD) [57] schemes for digital precoding"; with the ABB analog benchmark [58], all benchmarks are non-learned; no earlier learned precoder or standard network is compared.
q4_support: p. 11: "the computational complexity of the CMNN model is also determined based on FLOPs"; p. 14: "the proposed CMNN executes in only 22 ms" (Table V, p. 13).
q5_support: p. 11: "we generate 300000 data points for the train set and 20000 data points for the test set", its own simulated data; no link, DOI or availability statement for code or data appears.
notes: Area 3: the learned CMNN outputs the digital precoders; analog precoders and combiners come from analytical SVD-based designs. q2 counts only the 240 km/h test outside the 0-200 km/h training range (p. 15); the CSI levels 0.25 and 0.55 lie inside the trained range and are not counted, so the reviewer may confirm. q3 is 0: no earlier learned precoder is compared.
